title: Copy assignment
description:
Assignment (`b = a;`) is different from copy construction: `b` already exists and already owns an array, which must be released.

Write `Buffer& operator=(const Buffer& other)`. It must:

1. do nothing harmful when an object is assigned to itself (`a = a;`),
2. allocate the new array **before** deleting the old one (so that if allocation fails, the object is untouched),
3. copy the elements, free the old array, and return `*this`.
hints: Allocate and fill the new array into a local pointer first; only then `delete[]` the old one and take over the new one. That way a failed allocation leaves the object as it was.
